judge: Hard code asserts only, after normalizeDecision (the gate: verbatim evidence quotes, WhatsApp-only channel, valid send_at — a throw fails the case). Then: decision equals expected; for follow_up: channel is whatsapp, message_kind when listed, the message names 31.12.<taxYear> (unless mentions_valuation_date is false), at most max_question_marks (default 3) question marks, send_at is after `now` in the accountant's timezone, no substring of no_settled_rows_mentioned appears in the message; resolved_documents is exactly the listed id set (an object also pins each resolution), instances pins the per-row instance count, added_instances pins the number of instances added per catalog type (exactly the listed types; any row of the type may be the anchor), attestation equals the expected action, tax_fetch_action equals the decision's document-fetch action (null = none). message_includes / message_excludes are substrings the message must / must not contain; message_includes_any passes when at least one of its substrings appears. A file of the snapshot may carry holdings (the accounts list of the file check) and subject_name (null = no readable name). The optional verification_results (the verdicts that just landed, reasons read from the row) are shown in the VERIFICATION RESULTS block. Each case is a state snapshot: the client row, the checklist (explicit rows + every other catalog type seeded 'unresolved'), the thread, the optional unsent_drafts (the agent's own undelivered replies, shown in the UNSENT DRAFTS block) and the WhatsApp channel state, built into the exact prompt by buildPrompt() with the declaration-of-capital template.
